issue.title: [MRG + 2] Refactor kneighbors_graph and radius_neighbors_graph (et.al)
issue.body:
Following the discussion in https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/4019 this PR
1. Allows X to be None in `neighbors.kneighbors` which skips the first neighbor in both distance and connectivity mode.
2. Do not do anything special in other cases.

```
In [2]: knn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1).fit([[0], [1]])
In [3]: knn.kneighbors_graph([[0], [1]]).toarray()
Out[3]: 
array([[ 1.,  0.],
       [ 0.,  1.]])
In [5]: knn.kneighbors_graph([[2], [1]]).toarray()
Out[5]: 
array([[ 0.,  1.],
       [ 0.,  1.]])
In [8]: knn.kneighbors_graph().toarray()
Out[8]: 
array([[ 0.,  1.],
       [ 1.,  0.]])
In [6]: knn.kneighbors_graph([[2], [1]], mode='distance').toarray()
Out[6]: 
array([[ 0.,  1.],
       [ 0.,  0.]])
In [7]: knn.kneighbors_graph([[0], [1]], mode='distance').toarray()
Out[7]: 
array([[ 0.,  0.],
       [ 0.,  0.]])
In [9]: knn.kneighbors_graph(mode='distance').toarray()
Out[9]: 
array([[ 0.,  1.],
       [ 1.,  0.]])
```

Also, a happy 2015 to everyone!

I have done a PR along with a test to fix this issue. Refer to https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/4121

*Still new to open source, please advise if I missed anything

While working on the fix I discovered that the return values `dist` and `ind` arrays are inconsistent.
For KD Tree and Ball Tree, there is an extra dtype=object returned. Is this supposed to be the case? 

```
>>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(radius=1.6, algorithm='kd_tree')
>>> neigh.fit(samples) 
>>> print(neigh.radius_neighbors([1., 1., 1.])) 

(array([array([ 1.5,  0.5])], dtype=object), array([array([1, 2])], dtype=object))

>>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(radius=1.6, algorithm='brute')
>>> neigh.fit(samples)
>>> print(neigh.radius_neighbors([1., 1., 1.])) 

(array([[ 1.5,  0.5]]), array([[1, 2]]))
```

Thanks for the PR. It's more-or-less necessarily the case. For more than
one query point, the number of radius neighbors will almost always be
different per query, hence a 2d array cannot store them.

issue.title: [MRG] Fix boundary handling in radius_neighbors (issue #4072)
issue.body:
Fixes #4072 

This PR makes the `radius_neighbors` for brute force to include points lying on boundary of chosen radius. This is the same behavior as the KD Tree and Ball Tree `radius_neighbors`.

body: but it shouldn't be different depending on the algorithm, right?

Sorry, I didn't see that's what was being pointed out. Yes, shouldn't be inconsistent. I think we should either:
- always return array of arrays; or
- always return array of arrays , except when there's only one query

I expect the case that there happens to be equal number of radius neighbors is just too rare in practice; it shouldn't take the user by surprise. (Although perhaps, when expecting an array of arrays, there's not much surprising when a 2d-array turns up, i.e. the surprise only happens in the other direction? Any insights?)

+.5 for always returning a dtype object array.
As you say, this will happen "always" and having a special case doesn't make much sense.

As @amueller pointed out on another thread, this inconsistency is reported in #1400.

> this will happen "always" and  having a special case doesn't make much sense

Except when the number of queries is < 2, for which I think it's reasonable for the user to assume that they'll get back an array; and single-point queries are something we might expect.

issue.title: The datastructure returned by LSHForest.radius_neighbors should be consistent with the output of exact methods
issue.body: LSHForest has not been released yet. We should therefore fix this API consistency bug before the 0.16 release to avoid introducing a backward incompatible fix in the future.
